review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the uses of its declarations across the repo. I looked at the _value, _sandwich and endpoint theorem, and at the call sites in MagneticSquareInitial, MagneticSquareInverseConvex, MagneticTerminalCongruence and MagneticFieldInverseConvex. I found no loop or competing-rule risk. The one issue is that the only unfolding lemma for the Classical.choose-based definition has no simp attribute. I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether simp would apply this lemma in every position. The fieldScalarSquares side of the rewrite may also trigger further simp lemmas that I did not check. The rest of the file (the sandwich proof and the endpoint theorem) has no simp-interface issue that I could support.

findings.excerpt:
(magneticScalarSquareFourJet L hL i).value =
      fieldScalarSquares L (fun z => Real.log (Real.cosh z)) Real.tanh i :=
findings.problem: magneticScalarSquareFourJet is defined as a `.choose` of an existence proof. Its value is opaque to simp and `unfold`, so this lemma is the only way to reach the concrete function `fieldScalarSquares ...`. It has no `@[simp]` attribute. Every user must therefore name it by hand: `rw [magneticScalarSquareFourJet_value]` appears in MagneticSquareInverseConvex.lean (lines 20 and 31) and in MagneticSquareInitial.lean. It is also passed explicitly to `simp only [...]` in MagneticSquareInitial.lean (lines 21 and 46), MagneticSquareInverseConvex.lean (line 33), MagneticFieldInverseConvex.lean (line 44) and MagneticTerminalCongruence.lean (line 88). The rewrite goes from an opaque `.choose` term to a canonical concrete term, and the right side does not contain the left side, so it cannot loop. This is the canonical normal-form lemma for the definition, and it is not simp-tagged.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. Optionally also add a `toMagneticContinuationJet` version, `(magneticScalarSquareFourJet L hL i).toMagneticContinuationJet.value = fieldScalarSquares ...`, if simp does not already see through the parent projection. Then replace the explicit `magneticScalarSquareFourJet_value` arguments in the `simp only` calls with plain `simp`, or keep them where the unfolding must be controlled.
findings.benefit: Downstream goals that mention the square four-jet's value would normalise to `fieldScalarSquares` automatically. The recurring manual `rw`/`simp only` unfolding disappears, and there is one stable normal form for the choice-based definition.
